key_insight: A physics-guided LLM agent that reasons like a scientist—inferring physical properties (e.g., symmetries, invariances) then iteratively proposing and testing symbolic hypotheses—discovers interpretable governing equations more reliably than directly guessing formulas from data.
problem_solved: Existing LLM-based equation discovery systems typically guess equations directly from data and miss the multi-step scientific reasoning and physics constraints, producing spurious or poorly generalizing formulas.
method: Physics-guided LLM agent: infer physical properties (symmetries, invariances, conservation laws) from observations before proposing models.
Iterative scientist loop: generate hypotheses, design targeted experiments or queries, run symbolic regression, then verify and refine using physics priors.
Physics priors and symbolic verification prune the search space and improve robustness and interpretability of discovered equations.
impact: Enables more data-efficient, interpretable, and physically consistent equation discovery by combining LLM reasoning with domain priors—useful for scientific ML, modeling, and automated discovery workflows.
visual_elements: Agent loop flowchart: Observe → Infer physical properties → Propose symbolic equation → Design experiment → Verify/Refine
Before/after example: raw data plot vs. recovered symbolic equation with error bars and interpretability callouts
Search-space diagram: how physics priors (symmetry, invariance) constrain candidate equations
Performance chart: accuracy/data-efficiency comparison (physics-guided agent vs. direct-LM and baseline symbolic regression)
paper_title: Think like a Scientist: Physics-guided LLM Agent for Equation Discovery
paper_authors: Jianke Yang, Ohm Venkatachalam, Mohammad Kianezhad, Sharvaree Vadgama, Rose Yu
